# Introduction

Short- and subseasonal-horizon temperature forecasts drive energy demand
planning, frost alerts and agricultural scheduling in the Andes, where
elevation and aspect create large temperature differences between nearby
stations. Data-driven methods have become the default baseline for such
tasks: tree-based models for tabular regression and recurrent or temporal
convolutional architectures for sequence learning
 [@Reichstein2019; @SalinasDeepAR2020].

This paper contributes a reproducible benchmark of machine learning and deep
learning models for temperature forecasting on an Andean station network,
with a controlled ablation of anomaly decomposition as a preprocessing stage.
All results in this manuscript are produced by the pipeline under
`experiments/` and are listed in `manifest.yaml` as auditable claims.
